title: Entropy bound for protocol transcripts
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic protocol for disjointness on inputs of length $n$, and let $\mu$ be any measure on the hard sample space. The entropy of the transcript produced by running $p$ on the input pair generated by a sample, with respect to $\mu$, is at most the communication complexity of $p$ multiplied by $\log 2$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic protocol for disjointness on inputs of length $n$
$\mu$ is a measure on the hard sample space
replaced:
Fix $n \ge 1$, let $p$ be a deterministic two-party protocol for the disjointness
problem on inputs of length $n$, and let $\mu$ be any measure on the hard sample space.
Executing $p$ on the input pair generated by a sample produces a syntactic transcript,
and we regard this transcript as a random variable on the sample space. Then its Shannon
entropy, computed with respect to $\mu$, satisfies
\[
H[\text{transcript}] \;\le\; c(p)\,\log 2,
\]
where $c(p)$ is the communication complexity of $p$, i.e. the worst-case number of bits
exchanged.
